title: Varna 1. Mangalacharana
html:
The beginning of the varna is lost; homage to Chaitanya and Nityananda; Advaita — his roar and the Lord's descent; Gadadhara and Srivasa; Mahaprabhu's call to sing the Name of Hari; the glory of Jagadisha Pandita; the author's line of gurus — Raghunatha Acharya, Bhagavatananda (how he received his name), Premananda, Radhacharana; homage to the Gosvamis, the sixty-four mahantas and all Vaishnavas; the author's signature

Sri Sri Krishna Chaitanya is the refuge.
Sri Jagadisha-charita-vijaya.
The first varna.
Mangalacharana.

1…I attentively offer homage,1
if there be mercy on me, foolish, poor and lowly.

2Glory, glory to the son of Shachi, glory to the Merciful One!
Glory to Nityananda Raya, who descended as His prakasha!

Tatha hi:

3I worship Nityananda, from whose ears hang pearls, who in the form of Chaitanya's elder brother sanctified the face of the earth.

4Glory to Prabhu Nityananda, the abode of mercy!2
With devotion in my heart I worship His lotus feet.

5With a concentrated mind I have bowed to Chaitanya and Nitai:
see — there is no one else to deliver the living beings.

6Glory, glory to the merciful Sri Krishna Chaitanya!
Glory to Nityananda Raya, the son of Padmavati!

7Glory to Advaita Acharya, the king of devotees,
who spread prema-bhakti upon the earth!

Tatha hi:

8I worship Acharya Advaita, the Lord who descended as a devotee: having understood the disposition of His mind, Chaitanya descended to the earth.

9Prabhu Advaita Acharya is the avatara as a devotee;
bowing my head, I worship His feet.

10The avatara as a devotee is the Lord's non-different own form;
in many ways He destroys the darkness in the minds of living beings.

11For the deliverance of living beings He gives a thunderous roar;
at His roar the whole world was astonished.

12Night and day Prabhu ever roars;
at that roar the son of the king of Vraja appeared.

13Having appeared, the Lord gave Him an order;
receiving that order, He understood in His heart:

14"In Navadvipa, in Shachi's house, [My] descent will take place."
Knowing this, Prabhu Advaita was filled with boundless bliss.

15"Glory, glory to the son of Shachi, Sri Krishna Chaitanya!
After so many days the Lord has made Me blessed.

16Blessed, blessed am I — My birth has borne fruit;
I consider Myself blessed, having received the strength of [His] mercy."

17Thus Prabhu Advaita, by giving His roar,
Himself brought about the descent of Chaitanya.

Tatha hi:

18I worship Gadadhara together with Srivasa Pandita — the two vessels of Chaitanya's prema, who descended as [His] devotee and [His] shakti.

19Glory, glory to Gadadhara, the shakti of Chaitanya!
To his lotus feet I offer obeisances and praise.

20Srivasa Pandita is a dear devotee of Chaitanya;
see: his life is known throughout the world.

21Prostrating myself before those lotus feet, [I pray:]
"Prabhu, reveal the message of the truth to me, foolish and worthless."

22Prabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya, comprising the five tattvas,
has made His descent — blessed is the Kali-yuga!

23"The dharma of the Kali-yuga is the sankirtana of the Name of Hari:
raise your arms, call out 'Hari!' and dance!

24Hold in your heart the maha-mantra, the Name of Hari, as the essence:
apart from the Name of Hari, living beings have no other way."

25Speaking these words in a loud voice,
Mahaprabhu Himself, entreating, gives the Name of Hari to all without distinction.

26In this way He gave the order to His own devotees;
receiving the order, they all distributed the Name of Hari.

27Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya, the ocean of mercy!
In His mercy He delivered all the fallen.

28One branch of the Lord is Jagadisha Pandita;
see: his life is known throughout the world.

Tatha hi:

29I worship Prabhu Jagadisha, the friend of Duhkhini, maddened by prema for Chaitanya, grieved only by the sufferings [of others].3

30Glory, glory to Jagadisha! I have taken refuge [in him]:
in your mercy grant me your crimson feet.

31I am foolish and utterly low, and know nothing of bhajana;
be merciful to me, O treasure of Duhkhini's life!

32Prabhu is at every moment intoxicated with prema for Chaitanya;
day and night he says: "Gaura is the treasure of my life!"

33Raising his arms, Prabhu speaks these words:
"O living beings, with a concentrated mind take refuge in Chaitanya!

34Worship Chaitanya, take up the name of Chaitanya —
by worshipping Chaitanya all will attain deliverance!"

35He himself ever meditates on Chaitanya's feet;
calling out "Chaitanya!", Prabhu dances.

36Now he dances and sings, now he runs with his face turned upward,
now, falling in the dust, he rolls on the ground.

37"Sri Chaitanya, Sri Chaitanya is the treasure of my life!" —
saying this, he is beside himself with prema, be it night or day.

38If he sees someone poor, lowly, unhappy or distressed,
he himself offers him the jewel of Chaitanya's name.

39Be merciful, Jagadisha, protector of the world,
whose servant is Prabhu Raghunatha Acharya!

40What power have I to describe his praise?
Only for my own purification do I humbly say a little.4

Tatha hi:

41I worship the two feet of Raghunatha, the highest good, [him] whose name is the receptacle of the essence of all sweetness, who in the heart is everything.5

42Prabhu Raghunatha Acharya is an ocean of mercy:
in his mercy he delivered all the fallen.

43His name is the receptacle of the essence of all sweetness;
by his mercy bliss grows in the heart.

44The pair of his feet is the highest good;
to those feet I bow, relying on the strength of devotion.

45Whoever worships Raghunatha's feet with devotion,
he surely fulfils that one's heart's desire.

46A branch of Sri Raghunatha is Bhagavatananda,
whose mercy destroys the bonds of worldly existence for living beings.

Tatha hi:

47We worship him, the desired one — Srimad Bhagavatananda, the abode of bliss and virtues, the ocean of mercy.

48Glory, glory to Bhagavatananda Mahashaya!
Be merciful to me, the fallen one, O merciful Prabhu!

49Prabhu values virtues; he is the eyes of the blind;
to people without knowledge Prabhu gives knowledge of the truth.

50His boundless mercy cannot be described:
by his mercy the desires of the heart are fulfilled.

51Apart from those feet I know nothing else;
millions of times I prostrate myself at his feet.

52What can I, a fool, know of his life?
Formerly he was known by the name Sri Krishna.6

53He recited the "Bhagavata" right before the sri-murti;
hearing his recitation, the Lord was greatly pleased.

54Hearing from his lips the nectar of the "Bhagavata",
[the Lord] manifested Himself visibly from the sri-murti.

55At his words the Lord felt great joy
and, bringing His own cloth, placed it on his head.

56Seeing this, the devotees of Gaura rejoiced,
and all of them gave him the name Bhagavatananda.

57I, an insignificant being, am writing of all these events —
forgive me this fault in your mercy.

58I write the story of the mahantas from my heart's fond desire —
in your mercy forgive me this offence.

59I do not understand what I write — I am always bewildered;
whatever I write, I write only by the strength of your order.

60Prabhu, one of your branches is Srila Premananda,
by whose mercy living beings attain the highest bliss.

Tatha hi:

61I worship Premananda, who bestows divine knowledge on people covered by ignorance, whose heart is filled with compassion.

62Glory, glory to the venerable Gosani Premananda,
Prabhu, the ocean of the nectar of prema, full of all virtues!

63People covered by ignorance dwell in the well of worldly existence:
filling their bellies, they pass their time somehow or other.

64Like those blind from birth, they know nothing;
they cannot tell the proper from the improper; night and day are the same to them.7

65As a motherless child wanders about in sorrow,
so living beings come and go in vain in worldly existence.

66To all these living beings Prabhu gave divine knowledge
and in his mercy carried them across the river of worldly existence.

67The fear of worldly existence has troubled my mind;
bowing to your feet, I have taken refuge.

68I bow to your branch, Radhacharana Mahashaya,
by whose mercy living beings have bliss in their hearts.

Tatha hi:

69O Radhacharana, ocean of mercy, I, the lowly one, worship you: show mercy to me, worthless and blind, fallen into the cesspit of worldly existence.

70Glory to Prabhu Sri Radhacharana, the ocean of mercy!
For the deliverance of living beings you are [their] friend.

71Living beings come and go in the cesspit of worldly existence;
in that well of existence, in great darkness, I too remain.

72I am foolish and utterly ill-behaved, my mind ever wicked;
I am poor, lowly and base, and moreover devoid of bhajana.

73Show mercy, Prabhu — I have bowed to your feet;
deliver me from worldly existence — I have taken refuge.

Tatha hi:

74I worship that Radhika, clad in a cloud-coloured garment, whose radiance is [like] a steady streak of lightning, auspicious in form, dear to Sri Lakshmi.8

75The radiance of the feet surpasses steady lightning,
the beauty of the moons of the toenails surpasses the moon.

76Above them is a cloud-coloured garment, wondrously beautiful,
lovely to behold, worked with gold.

77With a joyful heart I have bowed to her feet;
I have no power to describe that form.

78In Vrajapura is the queen of Vraja, Radha Thakurani;
I know that this [Prabhu] is the embodiment of a part of her.9

79My remembrance, contemplation, vandana and bhajana
are to ever perform archana to those crimson feet.

80I am foolish, dull of mind and utterly ill-behaved;
apart from those feet I have no refuge.

81In offering praise I cannot tell merits from faults —
do not be angry at all with this foolish servant.

82I have offered a little praise to my own line of gurus;
now I shall glorify the Lord's devotees.10

Tatha hi:

83I diligently worship the beautiful feet of Sri Rupa, by which the fear of worldly existence goes far away.
Whoever serves those feet attains Sri Chaitanya:
show mercy to me, the ill-behaved.

84Glory, glory to Sanatana, the treasure of Chaitanya's life, renowned in this world!
Bowing my head, I worship the pair of his feet —
perhaps he will show me favour.

85Glory to Raghunatha Bhatta! Make me your own, worthless, devoid of bhajana and sadhana.
Worshipping your lotus feet, [may] I likewise give up the objects of the senses —
show mercy to me, foolish and worthless.

86Glory to Sri Jiva Gosani! I pray to you: give this fallen one the shade of your feet.
I have bowed to those feet — purify my mind,
show mercy by casting your merciful glance.

87Glory to Sri Gopala Bhatta! Mighty is the ocean of maya, and I am drowning in it.
Remove that maya, so that I may behold Vrajapura,
having given up the craving for the objects of the senses.11

88Glory to Raghunatha Dasa! May I become your servant — such is the desire of my heart.
Those feet take away sorrow, and before them I am poor and lowly —
I am a prisoner of the maya of samsara.

89From this maya of samsara drag me out, O Lord of the poor — there is no way but those feet!
I worship your two feet: remove the bad objects of the senses —
I pray at those feet.

90Glory to the sixty-four mahantas, the limit of whose virtues even the gods cannot see!12
My mind is very wicked, yet with all diligence
I have bowed to their feet.

91To all the residents of Navadvipa, the devotees of Sri Mahaprabhu, I bow, holding a straw between my teeth.
Forgiving my offences, may all be gracious
and fulfil my wish.

92The Vaishnavas who live in Vrindavana — I bow to their feet.
All the residents of Nilachala, the constant devotees of the Lord —
to them I bow with a concentrated mind.

93The servants of the servants of Mahaprabhu live in land after land — in the feet of them all I place my hope:
may I, birth after birth, attain those feet,
may I become a servant of the servants of the Lord's devotees.

94I bow to all the Vaishnavas — I have no power, and my intelligence is not subtle;
as far as my understanding goes I have praised all the Vaishnavas —
be kind and show mercy.

95The feet of Bhagavatananda are my wealth and fine treasure; his order came to me from above.
According to that Prabhu's wish, the life of Sri Jagadisha
has been described by Ananda Chandra Dasa.13

Thus, in the "Charitra-vijaya" of Sri Jagadisha Pandita, ends the first varna, called "Mangalacharana".

Notes

  1. The beginning of the varna is missing in the edition: the first leaf of the base manuscript is lost, and the text begins in the middle of a line ("…আমি বন্দি সাবধানে", …āmi bandi sābadhāne).
  2. The edition reads "করুনা সন্ম" (karunā sanma); taken as karuṇā-sadma, "abode of mercy" (rhyming with "পাদপদ্ম").
  3. A play on words: duḥkhinī-bāndhava is "the friend of Duhkhini" (Jagadisha's wife) and "the friend of the suffering [soul]". Duḥkhaika-kātaram — lit. "distressed only by suffering"; cf. 38.
  4. "কিছু করি পরিহার" (kichu kari parihāra): parihāra is taken in its Old Bengali sense of "humble entreaty, apology"; the rendering is tentative.
  5. The second line of the shloka is corrupt in the edition: "সর্ব্বমাধুর্য্য সারা নামাধী‹ং› হৃদয়েযৎ সর্বং" (sarva-mādhurya-sārā nāmādhī‹ṁ› hṛdaye yat sarvaṁ); it is translated by sense, following the Bengali paraphrase in 43.
  6. That is, Bhagavatananda's former name was Sri Krishna; the name "Bhagavatananda" ("the bliss of the 'Bhagavata'") was given to him for his recitation of the "Bhagavata" (53–56). To which Deity he recited is not said.
  7. Janama-āndhuyā (জনম আন্ধুয়া) — "blind from birth".
  8. The shloka is partly corrupt in the edition: "স্থিরবিদ্যুন্মতাকান্তিমম্বুদাম্বরধারিনীং। রাধিকাং শম্বরূপাং তাং শ্রীললক্ষীপ্রিয়াং ভজে" — "-মতা-" is taken as -latā- ("streak of lightning"), śambarūpāṁ as śaṁ-rūpāṁ ("auspicious in form"), śrīla-lakṣmī-priyāṁ as "dear to Sri Lakshmi"; the last two readings are unclear. The Bengali paraphrase (75–77) speaks of the radiance of the feet, the toenails and the garment.
  9. "তাঁর অংশ স্বরূপিনী ইহা আমি জানি" — aṁśa-svarūpiṇī (feminine), "the embodiment of her part". From the context (68–80: the homage to Radhacharana, into which the shloka on Radhika is inserted) the author apparently honours his guru Radhacharana as a partial manifestation of Sri Radha — in his eternal identity as Radha's maidservant (hence the feminine). The rendering "this [Prabhu]" is an interpretation; the original has "this" (ihā).
  10. The author's line of gurus (28–80): Jagadisha Pandita → Raghunatha Acharya → Bhagavatananda → Premananda → Radhacharana → Ananda Dasa. There follows homage to the Gosvamis and all Vaishnavas; "tatha hi" here introduces not a shloka but Bengali stanzas in tripadi.
  11. The edition reads "দেখিবেন ব্রজপুর" (dekhibena, lit. "he will see"); taken as "[that I may] see". "তিয়া গিয়া" — tiyāgiyā, "having given up".
  12. The sixty-four mahantas (cauṣaṭṭi mahānta) — the traditional Bengali Vaishnava count of the great associates of Sri Chaitanya.
  13. An expanded form of the author's signature; here he calls himself Ananda Chandra Dasa. "From above" — pratyādeśa, an order given in a dream or vision; the author tells of this dream at the beginning of varna 2.
